criterion: which fine-grained arxiv subject category (e.g. cs.LG, math.AG, hep-th) the paper title belongs to

categories.name: astro-ph
categories.definition: Papers on astrophysics, cosmology, stellar evolution, galaxies, and planetary systems.

categories.name: cond-mat
categories.definition: Papers on condensed matter physics, including superconductivity, disordered systems, and materials science.

categories.name: cs
categories.definition: Papers on computer science, including machine learning, software engineering, information retrieval, and computational linguistics.

categories.name: econ
categories.definition: Papers on economics, econometrics, finance, and market dynamics.

categories.name: gr-qc
categories.definition: Papers on general relativity, quantum cosmology, and gravitational waves.

categories.name: hep-ex
categories.definition: Papers on high energy physics experiments, detectors, and observational particle physics.

categories.name: hep-th
categories.definition: Papers on high energy physics theory, including string theory, quantum field theory, and quantum gravity.

categories.name: math
categories.definition: Papers on pure and applied mathematics, including algebra, geometry, analysis, and topology.

categories.name: nlin
categories.definition: Papers on nonlinear sciences, including chaotic dynamics, cellular automata, and pattern formation.

categories.name: physics
categories.definition: Papers on general physics, including fluid dynamics, optics, geophysics, and biophysics.

categories.name: q-bio
categories.definition: Papers on quantitative biology, including biomolecules, genetics, and neuroscience.

categories.name: q-fin
categories.definition: Papers on quantitative finance, including mathematical finance, risk management, and portfolio management.

categories.name: quant-ph
categories.definition: Papers on quantum physics, including quantum information, quantum optics, and quantum thermodynamics.

categories.name: stat
categories.definition: Papers on statistics, including machine learning methodology, probability theory, and statistical inference.
